clusters.name: Data Preparation Strategy
clusters.description: Which cleaning, validation, transformation, normalization, and indexing techniques prepare raw data for modeling?

relations.reading: Choices on Data Preparation Strategy limit the options available on Feature Management Strategy
relations.rationale: Preparation choices determine whether features are generated in pipelines, shared through a feature store, or retrieved from operational services.

values.label: ETL-based extraction and cleaning
values.description: Extracting and cleaning source data through recurring ETL processes.

values.label: Scripted reusable transformations
values.description: Encoding transformations as scripts or functions so they can be rerun on future datasets.

values.label: Automated validation and normalization
values.description: Validating incoming data against requirements, stopping on anomalies, and normalizing formats before training.

values.label: Schema-governed ETL indexing
values.description: Applying governed denormalization and indexing to categorical and ordinal fields during ETL.

values.label: Exploratory data profiling and validation
values.description: Using notebooks, attribute metadata, visual distributions, correlations, and user-defined checks to assess raw data.

values.label: Extract-load-transform processing
values.description: Loading extracted data before transforming it in the destination environment.

values.label: Immutable raw-data persistence
values.description: Incoming data is retained unchanged as an auditable source record for later processing and reproducibility.

values.label: Privacy-preserving data handling
values.description: Sensitive training data is anonymized, deleted, or protected during preparation and acquisition.

values.label: Dataset metadata cataloging
values.description: Preparation records dataset size, format, aliases, modification history, provenance, and access metadata.

clusters.name: Infrastructure Topology
clusters.description: Documents vary in hosting location, platform ownership, storage, networking, governance, and computational infrastructure supporting ML systems.

relations.reading: Choices on Infrastructure Topology limit the options available on Pipeline Triggering Strategy
relations.rationale: Available hosting and execution platforms limit how pipelines can be distributed, scheduled, and operated.

relations.reading: Choices on Infrastructure Topology affect the outcomes of Prediction Delivery Interface
relations.rationale: Infrastructure choices affect serving latency, scalability, reliability, compliance, and operational effort.

values.label: Hybrid on-premises and cloud infrastructure
values.description: ML environments combine internally managed infrastructure with cloud resources.

values.label: On-premises infrastructure
values.description: Organizations maintain and operate their own infrastructure and dedicated operational roles.

values.label: Managed cloud platform
values.description: Using managed cloud runtimes and provider-managed compute capabilities to host ML systems.

values.label: Container-orchestrated infrastructure
values.description: Hosting ML services and distributed processing through Kubernetes or alternative container orchestration.

values.label: Governed relational historical storage
values.description: Historical data is stored in an approved relational database such as Db2.

values.label: Specialized streaming platforms
values.description: Streaming technology is selected according to throughput, structure, latency, and workload characteristics.

values.label: Secure governed components
values.description: Component selection follows permissive licensing, HTTPS transport, and approval requirements for restricted technologies.

values.label: Vertically scalable compute-optimized training
values.description: Training primarily scales up on hardware optimized for compute and high single-threaded performance.

values.label: Local development serving infrastructure
values.description: Using a local development environment as a model-service deployment target.

values.label: Geographically resilient infrastructure
values.description: Using intercontinental availability, failover, and automated recovery to preserve service continuity.

values.label: Distributed multi-store infrastructure
values.description: Distributing offline, intermediate, and request-time results across stores chosen for workload needs.

values.label: Rejected Hadoop-based infrastructure
values.description: Hadoop-based infrastructure is explicitly declined.

values.label: Pluggable computation-resource abstraction
values.description: Separate ML code from computation resources so workloads can use clusters, distributed engines, or serverless backends.

values.label: Serverless compute infrastructure
values.description: Running ML workloads through managed serverless execution rather than directly managing underlying infrastructure.

values.label: Elastic compute scaling
values.description: Automatically scaling compute resources with changing data and workload demand.

values.label: Sharded data architecture
values.description: Partitioning data across shards to address availability, performance, and scalability demands.

values.label: Horizontal or vertical compute scaling
values.description: Scaling infrastructure by adding instances or increasing individual machine capacity.

values.label: Object storage for inference data
values.description: Persisting captured inference requests, responses, and metadata in object storage.

values.label: Sufficient data-platform infrastructure
values.description: Providing data-platform capability adequate for extraction, training, and serving.

values.label: Private human review workforce
values.description: Uses an organization-controlled workforce to review uncertain model predictions.

values.label: Serverless model serving
values.description: Exposing predictions through provider-managed functions rather than a continuously managed service.

values.label: Dynamic serving capacity
values.description: Automatically scaling prediction capacity as workload demand changes.

values.label: Virtual-machine-hosted secure data access
values.description: Host development access in virtual machines when local protected-data access is prohibited.

values.label: Edge-device inference infrastructure
values.description: Deploying model inference onto edge devices near data-producing or consuming systems.

values.label: Heterogeneous inference hardware
values.description: Selecting CPU, GPU, or FPGA resources as the computational substrate for inference.

values.label: Partitioned parallel data preparation
values.description: Dedicated parallel pipelines partition preparation workloads for scalable raw-data processing and feature engineering.

values.label: Federated hybrid-serving infrastructure
values.description: A server-held general model is combined with personalized models trained and served on user devices.

values.label: On-device model training infrastructure
values.description: User-specific models train locally on constrained edge devices without exporting personal training data.

values.label: Server-side aggregation of device updates
values.description: A central service aggregates device-trained model updates and redistributes an improved general model.

values.label: Federated learning framework
values.description: Infrastructure uses a framework supporting distributed data, constrained devices, and intermittent device availability.

values.label: Online data-source availability
values.description: Online computation depends on continuously available data sources and serving infrastructure.

values.label: Privacy-preserving model-update transmission
values.description: Devices transmit model updates without exporting personal training data.

values.label: Infrastructure hosting cost
values.description: Storage and serving infrastructure create material operating costs for ML systems.

values.label: Hardware bottleneck exposure
values.description: Infrastructure choices can create or avoid hardware bottlenecks affecting system cost and performance.

values.label: Storage query-latency-consistency trade-off
values.description: Storage architecture produces use-case-specific balances among query complexity, latency, and transactional consistency.

values.label: Sensitive-data protection constraint
values.description: Retaining private or sensitive data within governed organizational infrastructure.

values.label: Hybrid-cloud management complexity
values.description: Operational complexity resulting from managing cloud and on-premises infrastructure together.

clusters.name: Prediction Delivery Interface
clusters.description: How are predictions exposed, integrated, and coordinated across clients, applications, and model services?

relations.reading: Choices on Prediction Delivery Interface limit the options available on Infrastructure Topology
relations.rationale: Serving latency, scaling, security, and interface requirements restrict suitable hosting and infrastructure arrangements.

relations.reading: Choices on Prediction Delivery Interface affect the outcomes of Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Serving routes, rollout patterns, and human-review paths determine what production behavior can be observed.

relations.reading: Prediction Delivery Interface requires Model Packaging Format to be decided first
relations.rationale: The packaging representations in s19_p10 determine which inference engines and serving environments can expose models.

values.label: Real-time inference endpoint
values.description: A deployed model serves predictions through a real-time endpoint.

values.label: REST microservice serving
values.description: Model-system components expose prediction functionality through REST-based microservices.

values.label: Front-end prediction gateway
values.description: A front-end applies domain-specific logic between clients and the model-serving API.

values.label: Rejected strict microservice architecture
values.description: A strict microservice architecture for prediction delivery is explicitly declined.

values.label: Independently deployable ML microservices
values.description: Separate ML capabilities into independently deployable services integrated with applications through service boundaries.

values.label: API-mediated ML integration
values.description: Expose ML computation through an API while the application delivers the resulting prediction.

values.label: Openscoring serving framework
values.description: Use Openscoring as the production framework for fast, robust, flexible model serving.

values.label: Flexible inter-service dependency structure
values.description: Allow independently deployed services to interact with whichever other services their functionality requires.

values.label: Application-owned prediction delivery
values.description: Keep responsibility for delivering ML results in the application while the ML service focuses on producing predictions.

values.label: Mixed microservice-monolith integration
values.description: Combine microservices and monolithic components when product separation and shared data access both matter.

values.label: Pipeline-based batch scoring
values.description: Executing batch predictions through a machine-learning pipeline rather than an on-demand service.

values.label: Dedicated prediction service
values.description: A separate service derives features and handles prediction events for a model.

values.label: Threshold-based decision policy
values.description: A configured score threshold converts model output into an application decision.

values.label: Separated training and inference services
values.description: Keeping model training logic distinct from the prediction-serving interface.

values.label: Parameter-and-dataset job interface
values.description: Exposing data-intensive ML functions through parameter and dataset inputs with result outputs.

values.label: Asynchronous batch scoring interface
values.description: Exposes high-throughput scoring asynchronously, with results available after batch completion.

values.label: Score-result persistence and retrieval
values.description: Persists predictions in a dedicated store for later application retrieval or notification.

values.label: Asynchronous score notification
values.description: Delivers completed scores through push notifications, broker messages, or caller polling.

values.label: Request-specific model-version routing
values.description: Routes each inference request to the model version specified by the client.

values.label: Rejected monolithic ML application integration
values.description: Monolithic ML application integration is explicitly declined.

values.label: Asynchronous service-request coordination
values.description: Issue dependent user and demographic requests asynchronously to avoid summing request latencies.

values.label: Parameter-only model serving
values.description: Predictions are served from learned parameters or weights without retaining a complex model representation.

values.label: Authenticated model access
values.description: Prediction interfaces restrict model interaction to authorized users or services.

values.label: Model interaction interface
values.description: Models are accessed through APIs, user interfaces, command-line interfaces, or comparable interaction mechanisms.

values.label: Precomputed-result fallback
values.description: Serving falls back to stored predictions when online computation cannot satisfy response-time requirements.

values.label: Cascading feature-service dependencies
values.description: Dependent feature retrieval can create a chain of downstream microservice calls during serving.

values.label: Production-blocking model complexity
values.description: Outcome in which excessive model complexity prevents practical production use.

values.label: Independent feature-service integration
values.description: ML prediction services integrate as independently deployable components alongside product feature services.

values.label: Distributed ML-integrated development
values.description: Independent services enable development distributed across teams or components.

values.label: ML-integrated software scalability
values.description: Independent ML services improve scalability of the surrounding software product.

clusters.name: ML Testing and Validation Strategy
clusters.description: How are data, code, pipelines, models, deployments, and training-serving consistency tested and gated?

relations.reading: Choices on ML Testing and Validation Strategy limit the options available on Prediction Delivery Interface
relations.rationale: Evaluation gates, canary checks, and parity tests restrict which models can be promoted to serving.

relations.reading: Choices on ML Testing and Validation Strategy affect the outcomes of Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Validation baselines and thresholds determine which quality changes monitoring must detect after deployment.

values.label: Data-and-model CI validation
values.description: Continuous integration validates data, schemas, models, and software components.

values.label: Automated full-pipeline integration testing
values.description: The complete ML pipeline is triggered regularly and checked through every training stage.

values.label: Evaluator-gated model promotion
values.description: A model reaches the model server only after passing an independent quality evaluation.

values.label: Canary deployment validation
values.description: A candidate model is loaded into production serving and tested on realistic data before wider use.

values.label: Training-serving parity testing
values.description: Equivalent examples, scores, features, and predictions are compared across training and serving environments.

values.label: Checkpoint crash recovery testing
values.description: Interrupted training is tested for successful restoration from a checkpoint and continuation.

values.label: Deterministic training
values.description: Training is designed to produce reproducible models from identical data by reducing nondeterminism.

values.label: Automated feature-code unit testing
values.description: Unit-test feature-creation code to detect implementation defects.

values.label: Online A/B model validation
values.description: Compare a newly deployed model with an existing model on controlled online traffic before general release.

values.label: Versioned data artifacts
values.description: Version datasets and data artifacts alongside code to reproduce and compare training runs.

values.label: Rejected continuous testing as primary ML operations loop
values.description: Using continuous testing as the primary ML operations loop is explicitly declined.

values.label: Manual testing without continuous integration
values.description: Testing changes through notebook or script execution without a separate continuous integration process.

values.label: Holdout test evaluation
values.description: Evaluating a final trained model on a dataset withheld from training.

values.label: Business-objective model validation
values.description: Checking final model performance against the original business objectives before production use.

values.label: Code review for ML model specifications
values.description: Reviewing training code and model specifications before they are used operationally.

values.label: Pre-model evaluator implementation
values.description: Establish the evaluator before model construction.

values.label: Multi-level evaluation metrics
values.description: Gate models using prediction, application-impact, and system metrics.

values.label: Baseline model evaluation
values.description: Compare candidate models against a simple reference baseline, including heuristic baselines.

values.label: Training-validation dataset separation
values.description: Data is explicitly separated into training and validation sets before model fitting and evaluation.

values.label: Test-driven data-pipeline development
values.description: Data pipelines are designed and implemented with tests driving production code structure.

values.label: Data-product test fixtures
values.description: Purpose-built fixtures provide controlled data for automated tests of data products and pipelines.

values.label: Strategy-based dataset segregation
values.description: Training and evaluation subsets are produced through configurable sequential, random, shuffled, or custom strategies.

values.label: Fairness and protected-category testing
values.description: Validation examines fairness, bias, inclusion, and correlations between features and protected categories.

values.label: Model-staleness validation
values.description: Validation tests whether model age and outdated data reduce prediction quality or business impact.

values.label: Experiment reproducibility difficulty
values.description: Difficulty reproducing ML experiments despite tracking practices and supporting tools.

values.label: Multi-model evaluation complexity
values.description: Competing production models increase traffic-splitting, data-collection, and comparison complexity.

clusters.name: Workflow Execution Strategy
clusters.description: How are ML workflow stages represented, composed, conditionalized, and executed?

relations.reading: Choices on Workflow Execution Strategy affect the outcomes of Model Update Regime
relations.rationale: Execution decomposition, caching, and distributed execution affect training operation and reproducibility.

values.label: Componentized DAG orchestration
values.description: Separate, debuggable pipeline components are coordinated in a directed acyclic graph.

values.label: DSL-defined workflow graph
values.description: A domain-specific language specifies stage ordering and dependencies for ingestion, training, validation, and serving.

values.label: Function-based ML workflow composition
values.description: Represent ML workloads as parameterized functions and compose them into larger orchestrated workflows.

values.label: Pluggable workflow execution engines
values.description: Run workflow functions through interchangeable job, Kubernetes, Spark, or cluster execution engines.

values.label: Conditional pipeline progression
values.description: Use conditions to govern progression between training, validation, and deployment stages.

values.label: CRISP-DM iterative workflow
values.description: Structure data-science work as an iterative, bidirectional process through defined lifecycle phases.

values.label: Manual ML pipeline execution
values.description: Run preparation, validation, training, and testing manually before introducing higher automation levels.

values.label: Object-oriented workflow implementation
values.description: Organize multi-step machine-learning processing as maintainable object-oriented program structures.

values.label: Manual analysis workflow
values.description: Data and model analysis are performed manually before or during pipeline iteration.

values.label: Instrumented workflow execution
values.description: Workflow code is wrapped with logging and notification instrumentation for operational execution.

values.label: Runtime context parameter injection
values.description: Workflow execution injects runtime context and parameters into data-science code.

values.label: Cognitive and development cost
values.description: Workflow architecture affects cognitive overhead, development effort, readability, and organizational complexity.

values.label: Modeling effort misaligned with system utility
values.description: Outcome in which sophisticated modeling effort is wasted when problem definition, data, or deployment is neglected.

clusters.name: Serving Operations Strategy
clusters.description: How are models rolled out, scaled, reviewed, updated, and operated in production?

relations.reading: Choices on Serving Operations Strategy affect the outcomes of Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Rollout, review, scaling, and update practices determine which production monitoring signals and operational burdens arise.

values.label: Progressive production-first rollout
values.description: Models are designed for production from the outset and introduced progressively, using monitored testing such as A/B or canary rollout before full adoption.

includes.label: Progressive model rollout
includes.description: Traffic is gradually increased for a new model while performance and breakage are monitored.

includes.label: Production-first ML architecture
includes.description: Design the ML architecture around production requirements from initial development rather than retrofitting research artifacts.

values.label: Progressive containerized rollout
values.description: Production-oriented models are served in containers and exposed through a progressively expanded rollout, supporting repeatable deployment and operational scaling.

includes.label: Progressive model rollout
includes.description: Traffic is gradually increased for a new model while performance and breakage are monitored.

includes.label: Production-first ML architecture
includes.description: Design the ML architecture around production requirements from initial development rather than retrofitting research artifacts.

includes.label: Container-based prediction serving
includes.description: Deploying the prediction API in a container-based runtime.

values.label: Containerized prediction serving
values.description: Models are operated as containerized prediction services, with training separated from inference and a runtime API handling production requests.

includes.label: Container-based prediction serving
includes.description: Deploying the prediction API in a container-based runtime.

values.label: Cohort-based progressive validation
values.description: Candidate models are first exposed progressively to a selected test cohort, with behavior evaluated before broader rollout; the architecture is oriented toward production use.

includes.label: Progressive model rollout
includes.description: Traffic is gradually increased for a new model while performance and breakage are monitored.

includes.label: Production-first ML architecture
includes.description: Design the ML architecture around production requirements from initial development rather than retrofitting research artifacts.

includes.label: Test-cohort model rollout
includes.description: Selects a defined user cohort for evaluating candidate model behavior before broader exposure.

values.label: Human-in-the-loop coordinated redeployment
values.description: Production predictions can be routed to human reviewers, while updated models are redeployed across the serving fleet as part of coordinated operational updates.

includes.label: Human-review routing
includes.description: Low-confidence or below-threshold predictions are routed to human reviewers for correction or updating.

includes.label: Large-scale simultaneous model redeployment
includes.description: Redeploy updated models concurrently across many production servers.

values.label: Production-first fleet redeployment
values.description: The ML system is designed around production requirements and updated models are rolled out across many production servers, with deployment and performance monitored during the transition.

includes.label: Progressive model rollout
includes.description: Traffic is gradually increased for a new model while performance and breakage are monitored.

includes.label: Production-first ML architecture
includes.description: Design the ML architecture around production requirements from initial development rather than retrofitting research artifacts.

includes.label: Large-scale simultaneous model redeployment
includes.description: Redeploy updated models concurrently across many production servers.

values.label: Rejected model-instance load balancing
values.description: Model-instance load balancing is explicitly declined.

values.label: Reduced fraud-response latency
values.description: The serving architecture reduces the time from suspicious activity to an actionable model decision.

values.label: Maximum-request latency
values.description: Asynchronous requests yield total latency approximately equal to the slower request rather than the sum.

values.label: Real-time recommendation infeasibility
values.description: Heavy models combined with slow execution and feature-service calls can make real-time recommendations infeasible.

values.label: Fresh recommendation serving
values.description: Keeps recommendation results current as data and user actions change.

values.label: Low-latency recommendation serving
values.description: Produces recommendation responses quickly enough for interactive use.

values.label: Report-based prediction delivery
values.description: Predictions are delivered through reports, dashboards, webhooks, SMS, or email rather than direct synchronous serving.

values.label: Batch prediction delivery
values.description: Predictions are computed on a schedule and written to storage or analytics systems for downstream consumption.

clusters.name: Model Selection Strategy
clusters.description: How are candidate algorithms or models explored and selected during model development?

relations.reading: Choices on Model Selection Strategy affect the outcomes of Model Update Regime
relations.rationale: Algorithm exploration and rule-versus-ML selection affect how model training is conducted.

values.label: AutoML algorithm exploration
values.description: Training evaluates multiple algorithm choices automatically rather than selecting one manually.

values.label: Rule-based candidate selection
values.description: Selecting explicit heuristics or rules instead of a learned multivariable model for fraud decisions.

values.label: Neural architecture search
values.description: Explore candidate neural architectures using an explicitly selected architecture search space and evaluation process.

values.label: Random architecture exploration
values.description: Select candidate neural architectures randomly when the architecture space is small.

values.label: Gradient-based architecture exploration
values.description: Search neural architectures by converting the discrete space into a continuous, optimizable representation.

values.label: Evolutionary architecture exploration
values.description: Evolve candidate architectures by propagating successful variants and pruning weaker ones.

values.label: Ecology-aware model selection criterion
values.description: Include ecological cost or carbon footprint among criteria used to evaluate candidate architectures.

values.label: Performance-based model selection
values.description: Select the final model by comparative predictive performance after testing candidate models.

values.label: Automated hyperparameter optimization
values.description: Automatically search hyperparameters and training configurations rather than tune them manually.

values.label: Component-specific search algorithms
values.description: Use specialized search procedures for individual machine-learning pipeline components.

values.label: Explicit training hyperparameter configuration
values.description: Specifying training hyperparameters before launching model estimation.

values.label: Gradient-boosted tree model selection
values.description: Selecting an XGBoost gradient-boosted tree implementation for model training.

values.label: Managed estimator training interface
values.description: Launching training through a managed platform estimator API.

values.label: AutoML model blending
values.description: Combines AutoML-generated models with manually developed models during candidate construction.

values.label: Packaged off-the-shelf AutoML tool
values.description: Uses a boxed, commercial AutoML product as the primary modeling solution.

values.label: Interchangeable model algorithm library
values.description: Select from a modular library of replaceable algorithm implementations.

values.label: Linear learner selection
values.description: Linear or logistic learners are selected for efficient, responsive, explainable online learning.

values.label: Nonlinear learner selection
values.description: Nonlinear learners are rejected for online learning when their adaptation is too slow.

values.label: Single primary optimization metric
values.description: Teams optimize one shared most-important metric to avoid conflicting objectives.

values.label: Manual hyperparameter tuning
values.description: Hand-set hyperparameters optimized through trial and error.

values.label: Heuristic rule complexity
values.description: Rule-based fraud selection becomes unwieldy as fraud vectors grow complex and evolve.

values.label: Explainable and reproducible model results
values.description: Seek model-selection processes that produce interpretable and repeatable results for development and regulated use.

values.label: Linearity limitation
values.description: The linearity assumption limits the functions representable by a selected linear learner.

values.label: Rapid adaptation to changing data
values.description: A responsive learner adapts quickly when data distributions or conditions change.

values.label: Linear-model implementation simplicity
values.description: Linear learners provide efficient implementations and straightforward incremental update rules.

values.label: Linear-model prediction explainability
values.description: Linear learner predictions are easier to explain than predictions from black-box models.

values.label: Accuracy-speed objective tension
values.description: Predictive accuracy and response speed receive different priority depending on application context.

values.label: User-engagement metric misalignment
values.description: Product engagement measures may diverge from model accuracy or speed objectives.

values.label: AutoML underperformance relative to human baseline
values.description: Outcome in which evaluated AutoML solutions score below a manually constructed baseline.

clusters.name: ML Release Automation
clusters.description: How are ML builds, tests, deployments, releases, and handoffs automated across the lifecycle?

values.label: Production build-script automation
values.description: Use build scripts to automate conversion of developed ML code into deployable workloads.

values.label: Production test-script automation
values.description: Use test scripts as an automated gate before a workload is considered production-worthy.

values.label: Lifecycle event notification
values.description: Teams receive alerts for experiments, registrations, deployments, and drift events.

values.label: Unified ML and software release process
values.description: Treats models and surrounding application services as software assets in one coordinated release process.

values.label: Lifecycle-wide ML automation
values.description: Automate integration, testing, release, deployment, infrastructure management, and training across the ML lifecycle.

values.label: Automated model-creation service
values.description: Expose model creation as a dedicated service that builds candidates from data and evaluation criteria.

values.label: Automated model engineering pipeline
values.description: Training, evaluation, testing, and packaging are automated as one repeatable workflow.

values.label: Data-science-to-engineering model handoff
values.description: Transferring trained model artifacts from data scientists to engineers for deployment.

values.label: Infrequent model release cadence
values.description: Releasing or retraining production models only occasionally, such as a few times per year.

values.label: Manual model deployment
values.description: Deploying a trained model artifact manually rather than through continuous delivery.

values.label: Continuous delivery pipeline
values.description: Automated release pipeline that continuously builds, tests, and deploys ML changes.

values.label: Research-to-production lead time
values.description: Time required to move an ML model from research into production.

values.label: Rapid model profitability
values.description: Packaged operational infrastructure can shorten delivery to profitable models.

values.label: Seamless production operation
values.description: Outcome of operating ML systems smoothly after deployment.

values.label: Visible machine-learning gains
values.description: Outcome in which ML benefits are visible to stakeholders.

values.label: User satisfaction
values.description: Outcome in which production ML systems satisfy users.

clusters.name: Production Monitoring Strategy
clusters.description: Documents vary in which technical, behavioral, business, fairness, drift, and operational signals are monitored and how feedback triggers action.

relations.reading: Choices on Production Monitoring Strategy affect the outcomes of Model Update Regime
relations.rationale: Monitoring results can trigger retraining, new experiments, or changes to training data and schedules.

values.label: Continuous production model-performance monitoring
values.description: Ongoing monitoring of model behavior and performance after deployment.

values.label: Statistical drift analysis
values.description: Production distributions are compared with training distributions to detect data drift.

values.label: Disaggregated performance monitoring
values.description: Performance is assessed across critical regions or groups rather than only through aggregate accuracy.

values.label: Business and decision-quality monitoring
values.description: Monitoring evaluates whether model-enabled decisions support application goals and acceptable outcomes.

values.label: Fairness and non-accuracy monitoring
values.description: Fairness, ethics, stability, explainability, user experience, and edge-case behavior receive ongoing oversight.

values.label: Automated retraining triggers
values.description: Schedules or monitoring events trigger new pipeline executions or experiment cycles.

values.label: Real-time user and business feedback analytics
values.description: Monitoring user behavior and business signals to evaluate decisions and guide subsequent changes.

values.label: Lifecycle-wide ML monitoring
values.description: Monitor ML system construction and operation across all lifecycle stages, not only deployed model accuracy.

values.label: Software-metrics-only monitoring
values.description: Monitoring limited to generic software metrics without model-specific signals.

values.label: Business-KPI-only monitoring
values.description: Monitoring limited to downstream product or business KPIs without timely model signals.

values.label: No active model-performance monitoring
values.description: Operating deployed models without actively tracking predictions, actions, or performance.

values.label: AIOps-based IT operations response
values.description: Applies AI to detect and proactively respond to day-to-day IT operational issues.

values.label: Centralized observability logging
values.description: A centralized collector gathers operational and model-monitoring logs for unified observability.

values.label: Search-indexed monitoring storage
values.description: Collected monitoring data is stored in a searchable index for querying and analysis.

values.label: Visual monitoring dashboard
values.description: A visual interface presents indexed monitoring information for operational exploration.

values.label: Scheduled hourly monitoring
values.description: Monitoring jobs run on a fixed hourly schedule after sufficient endpoint traffic accumulates.

values.label: Research-phase model remediation
values.description: Detected production deterioration can send work back to research for a remade model.

values.label: Input-and-response model monitoring
values.description: Monitoring jointly examines model inputs and responses when ground truth and business effects are delayed.

values.label: Aggregate-metric failure masking
values.description: Stable aggregate accuracy can conceal degradation in a critical subset of production data.

values.label: Feedback-loop bias amplification
values.description: Biased production feedback can be recycled into retraining and progressively increase model bias.

values.label: Business and financial impact of inaccurate predictions
values.description: Inaccurate production predictions cause poor decisions and financial losses.

values.label: Production input and infrastructure disruption
values.description: Erroneous inputs, outages, demographic changes, and broken pipelines disrupt deployed model operation.

values.label: Prediction unreliability from unusual inputs
values.description: Erroneous or unusual live inputs produce unreliable predictions and prediction failures.

values.label: Operational damage from model decay
values.description: Model failure or degradation can cause user-facing harm and financial loss.

values.label: Data-bias-driven model retraining
values.description: Outcome in which biased data invalidates a model and necessitates retraining.

clusters.name: Feature Construction Strategy
clusters.description: Which feature-engineering approach determines the inputs supplied to models?

relations.reading: Choices on Feature Construction Strategy limit the options available on Model Update Regime
relations.rationale: Feature inputs and target identification determine what training regime can consume and evaluate.

values.label: Domain-informed feature engineering
values.description: Combining raw data with domain knowledge to construct additional model features.

values.label: Rich contextual feature inputs
values.description: Adding behavioral and contextual signals such as communities, clicks, likes, or time-related variables.

values.label: Iterative feature experimentation
values.description: Generating, testing, and accepting or discarding features through repeated experiments.

values.label: Target-attribute identification
values.description: Identifying the supervised-learning target and relevant attributes before feature construction.

values.label: Automated feature engineering
values.description: Use automated search or transformation to generate and select model features.

values.label: JSON feature representation
values.description: Represent features in JSON so loading and transformation can generalize by feature names and types.

values.label: Feature bucketing and missing-value transformation
values.description: Transform raw features through bucketing or binning and replace missing values before training.

values.label: Multi-source feature integration

values.label: Compact embedded model deployment

values.label: PMML algorithm-coverage limitation

values.label: Model-format interoperability limitation

values.label: Serialized-model compression

values.label: Model-format vendor dependence

values.label: Serverless artifact-size constraint

values.label: ONNX serving performance gain

clusters.name: Notebook Development Workflow

values.label: Rejected containerized notebook environment

values.label: Avoided cloud-hosted notebook execution

values.label: Standalone Python project workflow

values.label: Fixed data-snapshot reproducibility

values.label: Duplicated notebook query logic

values.label: Notebook execution-result history

values.label: Version-controlled notebook caches

values.label: Cloud-hosted notebook execution

values.label: Web-based notebook development interface

values.label: Standalone sharable notebook documents

values.label: Rich media notebook integration

values.label: Language-agnostic notebook architecture

values.label: Automated notebook-code testing

values.label: IDE-integrated notebook development

values.label: Stale cached state

values.label: Notebook reproducibility variation

values.label: Accumulated untracked notebooks

values.label: Notebook technical debt

values.label: Independent model-version updates
